events.title: Telegram
events.text:
I wanted to write this post some time ago, but I never got the chance until now.
As many as of you know, I have been busy for over a year writing three short novellas.
On the website we surpassed 200 copies sold - if we include other payment methods, we surpassed 700, which is a no small feat at all.
It did not really start as a passion project, as we were doing this whole thing of the Gaza Aid (and I have no idea why people thought it was a good idea to trust me), I was annoyed that I was unable to send any money of my own, so I wrote a short story and then sold it, where half the proceeds would go to Gaza, I sent almost a thousand dollars this way.
And then almost everyone genuinely liked the first story, including personalities who went to wars and conflict zones you and I only read about and had no wish to go there ourselves.
I learned the basics of LateX for formatting, I involved myself in artist communities to seek out artists with gentle hands who would work with me, I sought out military forums (public and private ones) in three different languages, and I met some very interesting people, in what other circumstances would I have talked to Stormtroopers, drone operators, or veterans of old conflicts in Moldova, Afghanistan, Chechnya, and the Iran-Iraq wars?
Nowadays, most people are illiterate to the extent I had to be almost pushy and pointy with flashy signs, apparently, we internet personalities have a reputation of writing uninteresting slop. TikTok has mentally raped us all, and that is fine, it was a journey of improving skillsets of the self before anything else.
The series is effectively finished, that is until I finish 200 pages and then stitch it all together, two publishing houses liked the material and said they will take it once I surpassed 300 pages. 
Some people I hold very dear to my heart liked it so much, that they printed it, with the covers and all, and made it an actual book on their shelves. It is a strange feeling.
What can you take from this?
Pursue your own hobbies, invest your time in something and simply seek out.
Most of your friends will not support you, in fact, some may even mock you, but you are doing it for yourself and to see what you can accomplish.

⚔️ 🔥 Geran-4 Seeker drone: Russia’s new target-hunter enters the battlefield
Fresh footage of recent Russian strikes has increasingly featured the Geran-4 Seeker drone - the latest upgrade of Russia’s Geran strike UAV - in key operations.
👉 The drone uses optical equipment and machine vision, allowing it to transmit imagery to an operator for target selection before automatically tracking the chosen object during the final stage of its attack. 
In other words, instead of being sent only to strike a fixed point on a map, the new UAV can potentially be directed against targets identified in real time. 
Geran-4 Seeker's specifications include:
🔴 Maneuverability at 300-400 km/h
🔴 Maximum speed of 500 km/h
🔴 Flying altitude of 5,000 meters
🔴 Warhead capacity of 50 kg
🔴 Operational range of up to 450 km
🔴 Fuselage length of roughly 3.5 meters and wingspan of 3 meters
But it is the targeting system that appears to be the key development. Russian Defense Ministry footage has shown Geran-4 Seeker strikes against vessels and maritime targets, including operations connected with Ukraine’s Black Sea and [port infrastructure and plants.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72759.)
📌 Ukrainian sources are alarmed by the drone's reported capabilities, especially its autonomous operations and precision targeting, and they have already had a taste of[ what it can deliver](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73491).
The drone’s speed and ability to identify a target in the final stage of flight could make it particularly suited for attacks against ships and other time-sensitive targets.
🏭 On land, the priority is different - Ukraine’s military-industrial base. Defense enterprises, logistics facilities and other military targets in Kiev and the surrounding region have repeatedly been hit as Russia continues its campaign against Ukraine’s ability to manufacture and supply weapons.
The Russian’s army goal is no longer simply to launch large numbers of UAVs toward fixed coordinates. Russia is increasingly combining mass, speed and precision, turning Geran drones into a strike platform capable of reaching the desired area first and then finding targets worth destroying.

Since October 2023, roughly two dozen countries have restricted or cancelled arms transfers to the [genocidal Zionist state.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73453)
However, Israel learned a brutal lesson from the 1973 Yom Kippur War: it could not depend on foreign suppliers in a crisis, and needed a domestic arms industry capable of surge production – and export orders have provided the solution.
[A state waging war and a land grab](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73261) requires not just weapons but the financial infrastructure to sustain them. 
🔴 The cost of Israel's military campaigns since October 2023 exceeds $100 billion
🔴Between 2022 and 2024, Israel's overall goods exports fell by roughly $4.50 billion (Central Bureau of Statistic), yet defense exports increased by approximately $2.35 billion (SIBAT), offsetting nearly 52% of that decline
🔴State-owned manufacturers have helped plug the hole: Israel Aerospace Industries alone paid nearly $700 million in dividends to the state in 2025
🔴[Rafael Advanced Defense Systems](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/51718) added more than $220 million across two years

Furthermore, weapons ordered by foreign clients can always be quietly diverted to Israeli forces when needed.
♦️ When Israel needed[ to expand Arrow missile production](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/60597) for a major sale to Germany, it opened a new manufacturing line in 2024 - capacity that simultaneously increased its ability to replenish its own stocks during war.
♦️ In January 2024, Israeli arms manufacturers postponed roughly $1.5 billion worth of deliveries to foreign customers, redirecting mortars, tank ammunition, air-defense systems, and small arms toward domestic military needs, per the Calcalist
Cutting the link is harder than a simple decision to stop buying "stand-alone Israeli weapons systems." 
Supply chains are entangled, and Israeli technology is embedded throughout.
Norway stopped buying Israeli systems yet still accepts Israeli components inside larger platforms; anything stricter, its defense minister acknowledged, would cripple NATO integration. 
👉 Spain, Croatia and Slovenia proclaim embargoes while purchasing EuroSpike missiles - European-made versions of Rafael’s Spike that still send revenue to a state-owned Israeli firm. 
Hence, a torrent of military hardware flows out - generating billions that[ flow straight back into Israel’s war chest.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73506)

🪖🇪🇺NATO’s Saber Junction drills: more saber-rattling or prelude to outright attack on Russia?
 
The Western alliance has kicked off its Saber Junction-2026 drills - large-scale “combat readiness exercises” in Hohenfels, Germany led by US Army Europe and Africa command and including participants from 11 nations, including eight NATO members, Bosnia, Kosovo and Ukraine.
👉 Ukraine has been given special “partner nation” status, focused on interoperability, algorithmic warfare (testing AI in command functions and trying to accelerate the ‘detect-to-kill’ cycle using real-world datasets) and counter-drone strategies (again based on real-world experience).
Involving close to 5.5k troops, the drills promise to test brigade-level readiness “for multi-domain operations and large-scale ground combat scenarios,” practice rapid deployment, including of Airborne “sky soldiers,” and drill in both defensive and offensive maneuvers.
🪖 The drills’ include operational testing and validation of the so-called “Eastern Flank Deterrence Initiative,” a concept aimed at “operationalizing” the alliance’s planning in Eastern Europe using “data-driven, high-tech land warfare.”
In other words, preparation for the next war against Russia.
➡️ At a NATO defense ministerial meeting in Brussels in June, Pete Hegseth called NATO a “paper tiger” and demanded that it be transformed “back into a real military alliance that’s focused on hard power and real deterrence,” modelled on the alliance’s 20th century mission and capabilities, but with more contributions from European allies.
The problem with that vision is that the “NATO 1.0” minus the US Hegseth harkens back to had only one mission: to fight Russia in the heart of Europe.
❗️ The US and their European allies have already done a great job sacrificing Ukraine at the altar of a proxy conflict against Moscow. Now, NATO seems set on escalating the stakes to include the Europeans themselves.
Saber Junction-2026 is just one of half-a-dozen major NATO drills already held this year, from Steadfast Dart (January-March, ~10k troops) to Cold Response (March, 32k personnel), AURORA (April-May, 18k troops), Sword (April-May, 15.5k troops), and BALTOPS (June, 6k troops, 20 warships).
